react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on Galactose Metabolism as the overwhelmingly dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP reported Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182, FDR 7.52×10⁻¹⁵) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, FDR 7.52×10⁻¹⁵) as the top two hits with five shared driver metabolites: galactitol (KEGG:C01697), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137) and sucrose (KEGG:C00089). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the identical KEGG:hsa00052 Galactose Metabolism (p = 5.65×10⁻⁹) with the same five compound hits, achieving cross-paradigm consensus at rank 1 in two independent tools. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked galactose metabolism at rank 4 (p = 0.0077) and also identified phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (MUMM:phosphatidylinositol_phosphate_metabolism, p = 0.0021), a pathway in which myo-inositol and glycerol serve as structural precursors for phosphatidylinositol head-group biosynthesis. The pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid, detomidine and phenylacetic acid did not map to any significantly enriched pathway, consistent with a primary metabolic signal centred on carbohydrate handling. Glycerol and myo-inositol are driver metabolites shared between the galactose and glycerophospholipid / inositol-phosphate modules, suggesting the treatment perturbs both galactose catabolism and downstream lipid signalling simultaneously.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms identify galactose metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactose Metabolism as the top hit across SMPDB and KEGG with FDR = 7.52×10⁻¹⁵, driven by five shared metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identified KEGG:hsa00052 at rank 1 with p = 5.65×10⁻⁹, hitting the same five compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct returned Galactose metabolism at rank 4 with p = 0.00798, confirming pathway involvement at the mass-spectral level. The five driver metabolites are galactitol, galactinol, glycerol, myo-inositol, and sucrose; all five are documented members of the KEGG galactose metabolism module. Secondary hits include Phenylalanine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00360, p = 0.0298) with phenylacetic acid, and Amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism (KEGG:hsa00020, p = 0.034) with myo-inositol, indicating ancillary perturbations beyond the primary signal.
